newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss banks could cooperate abroad - senior banker.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks could cooperate abroad - senior banker.

text.p: Big Swiss banks might soon join forces abroad to boost their strength on international markets while still competing at home, a senior Swiss banker suggested on Friday.

Swiss Bank Corp (SBC) Chairman Georges Blum told the Swiss Trade and Industry Association's (SHIV) annual meeting in Lausanne that he did not think any big bank would sell off its Swiss retail banking business to a competitor.

"This is really a core business for a universal bank where the specialised customers of tomorrow are acquired, be it in the areas of lending, investment or financial services," he said, according to the text of his speech distributed in Zurich.

"On the other hand, the potential for synergy among the big banks is apparently very great, and pooling resources -- especially in the international area -- would make it possible to compete more strongly on international markets," he said.

"Thus it is not absurd (to suggest) that in five to 10 years two of the big banks will possibly -- and I stress possibly -- work together more closely, that is, join forces in certain specialised areas," he said.

SBC chief executive Marcel Ospel has been quoted in recent newspaper articles saying that he intends to focus a great deal of his attention on the bank's domestic business during the next 12 to 18 months.
The domestic media has been speculating that Ospel intends to shut down a majority of the bank's domestic branches or even sell off its traditional small customer business.

Blum said Switzerland was still "overbanked" with one branch for every 1,900 residents despite a decline in the number of branches over the past five years. Regional and cantonal banks faced special challenges to reshape their businesses.

The three big banks -- SBC, Union Bank of Switzerland and Credit Suisse, a unit of CS Holding -- "have a big enough market share in Switzerland and abroad to be able to operate profitably in parallel", he said.
Only if one of them would sustain heavy losses or make big strategic errors could it be taken over, he added.

Talk of a mega-merger among banks in Switzerland has been bandied about since CS Holding, the nation's second-largest banking group, approached UBS in April. UBS, Switzerland's biggest bank, rebuffed the advance.
